blocking_issues.title: Company profit and company margin are only right for whole calendar months, but Home and Profit show them for any days
blocking_issues.where: Home (This month), /profit with any date range, GET /api/v1/company-bridge
blocking_issues.repro: Company costs sit on the one day they are dated and are not spread over the month. 1. /profit?from=2026-10-01&to=2026-10-31: company costs 7,050,000 cents, overhead gap 507,580, company profit 15,271,316 (23.0%). 2. /profit?from=2026-10-02&to=2026-10-31, one day less: company costs 0, overhead gap null, company profit 14,795,028 (23.6%). The popover says 'No company costs were typed in for these days, so Pulse trusts the overhead inside your hourly rates', but the tile still says 'Company margin 23.6%, After overhead and paid time not on any job'. 3. /profit?from=2026-11-10&to=2026-11-16: Job margin 25%, Company margin 23.5%, with no overhead step at all. 4. Oct 20 to Nov 18 (last 30 days): one month of costs (7,050,000) against 30 days of rate overhead (7,722,427), so the gap is -672,427 and it adds $6,724 to company profit. 5. Home, This month, Nov 1 to Nov 18: the full $70,500 for November is charged against 18 days, so $15,057 comes off and Company margin reads 21.7%. For all of October the same step was only $5,076.
blocking_issues.why_it_matters: The company number was the round three fix, and it is right at month close. But I look at Home every morning, and there the month to date company margin is too low early in the month and jumps around by date range. A week view says 'after overhead' when no overhead was checked. Finance will see three different company margins for October depending on the first day picked. Spread company costs by day, or show the company number only for whole months and say so on the tile.

blocking_issues.title: Warehouse extra services come in as revenue with no hours and no cost, so they show a 100% margin with no warning
blocking_issues.repro: Open /services. The services made by the warehouse sync read: Programming (hours), 5 hours, $195.00 revenue, $0.00 cost, 100%. Grade B Pallet $72.50, $0.00, 100%. Customer Pickup $50.00, $0.00, 100%. Return Additional Item $16.00, $0.00, 100%. The Check column is empty for all four. In the database all 13 wms entries have hours 0 and labor_cost_cents 0. blocking_issues.why_it_matters: Rollups still reconcile and nothing is counted twice, I checked. But $753.50 of pure profit landed in job profit, and firmware work billed by the hour clearly took someone's time. In a real shop with hundreds of warehouse service records a month, the service table would say these are my best services when nobody has costed them. Flag them 'no hours logged', or cost them at the service standard, and keep them out of the margin ranking until then.

blocking_issues.title: One tap deletes a whole day of work on the job Work log, with no question

blocking_issues.title: Small wording and label slips
blocking_issues.where: /settings/close, job Work log, company profit popover, Log work grid
blocking_issues.repro: 1. October shows the badge 'Ready to close' right above '1 step needs fixing before these numbers can be trusted' and a 'Fix this first' step. 2. The Entries crew cell reads 'Line lead 8, 1 people'. 3. The company profit popover for Nov 10 to Nov 16 lists 'less Time not on a job that no job carried -$36.17', a minus on a 'less' line, next to 'less Paid time not on any job $2,948.87' with no minus. 4. best_things: Everything still reconciles to the cent, now with warehouse services flowing in. For three date ranges, 8 different cuts each matched the summary on 7 money fields and hours with 0 difference, and matched the raw database sums.

Job delete is now safe and honest. The dialog names the dollars and hours that will leave, the default button is 'Keep the job', and Restore put my job back into every rollup to the cent, with company profit back to 11,057,415 cents exactly.

Month close now shows the number I would lock: job profit, the three steps down, and company profit, and the saved snapshot equals the live company bridge. A job with rows in a closed month cannot be deleted.
The multi labor type day form is right on the math, saves all lines or none, and edit, delete and undo act on the whole day. Money stays hidden from the supervisor on the screen and in the API.
CSV round trips are the best I have used: 16 streams exported and checked back in with every row 'unchanged', even with entry ids blanked, and look alike rows are skipped by default.
The warehouse sync is safe to run again and again. Two syncs in a row changed nothing, closed months are left alone, and the screen says how many records came in and how many have no price.
Quote vs actual with a waterfall that adds up exactly to the gap is still far past what Easy Metrics gave me.
Plain words everywhere. Every round two copy slip I named is fixed.
what_would_wow_me: Fix the company number for part months and I am close to signing with no caveats. (1) Spread company costs over the days of their month, or show company profit only for whole months and label it. Home on day 2 of a month should not charge the whole month's rent. (2) Give warehouse extra service entries a cost, or flag them 'no hours logged' and keep them out of the service margin ranking, and count unpriced client level entries in Home 'Things to fix'. (3) Ask before deleting a day of work, and make the edit and delete icons bigger and further apart on a tablet. (4) Remove the grey 4 and 32 from the day form and use the same hours check as the Log work grid. (5) Send scheduled reports and urgent alerts by email. (6) Clean up the small label slips, 'Ready to close' next to 'needs fixing' first. If I also saw a brand new empty org reach a first job profit number in 10 minutes, I would be wowed.
verdict_paragraph: Round three fixed what I asked for. Five of my six round two issues are fixed and proven by hand, and the sixth, email, is deferred by plan. Month close now shows job profit and company profit, and the snapshot it saves equals the company bridge to the cent. Job delete asks first and tells me the dollars, and restore put my test job back into all 8 rollups with company profit exact to the cent. Warehouse extra services now flow into revenue, a second sync adds nothing, and every rollup still reconciles with no double count. The new multi labor type day form gets the math right and saves all or nothing. I score Pulse 88 against an estimated 52 for Easy Metrics, with every category at 8 or higher, so it is clearly the better product. I am still not wowed, for one main reason. The company number is only right for a whole month. Change October by one day and overhead drops out. Look at a week and the tile says 'after overhead' when no overhead was checked. On Home, the month to date company margin carries the whole month's rent from day 2. That is the number round three was built to make trustworthy, and I open Home every day, not month close. The other new findings are small: warehouse services show a 100% margin because they carry no cost, a whole day of work can be deleted with one tap, and grey sample numbers came back in the new form. I would sign once the part month company number is fixed or clearly limited to whole months.

lens: Staff engineer and solutions architect, technical due diligence: integration depth with Portal, CRM, WMS and Projects in both directions, standalone mode, math against raw rows, data integrity under concurrency, money hiding for no money roles on every route and page payload, security and operations. How I tested: Node scripts against the production build on port 3500 with one saved session per user (admin, j.okafor, cs.team, maya), my own SQL on the local database, Playwright for 50 pages per user, direct calls to server actions, and vitest. I walked 290 GET URLs under /api/v1 for each of three users. What I could not test: the off plan link chip in a browser (the server runs with ENTITLEMENTS_DEV_ALLOW_ALL=1 and I may not restart it, so I used the domain tests and read the code), a real month close (I did not close a month, I read the snapshot another critic made for October), and Projects and WMS changes through their own screens (I changed pm.time_entries, wms.vas_operations and wms.billing_fees rows by SQL, which is what Pulse reads). Email delivery is deferred and not scored. Easy Metrics scores are the section 5 estimates from public evidence, not hands on. Cleanup: the probe database role se_probe was dropped and its grants removed. My test warehouse record and my two test Projects time rows were deleted. The Apex contract rate is back at 2.75 and the price row it made on WO000094 was removed in the app. Left behind, all soft deleted: jobs J-1044 and J-1045, clients Harbor Roast Collectiv, Harbr Roast Collective and SE3 Origin Probe Zq, the work rows on J-1045, one warehouse service entry with source_ref wms:vas:se-test-0001, and one Projects labor row on J-1007 for 2026-11-16. Also left: audit log rows, sync run rows, and the core schema ACL now reads postgres=UC/postgres, which is the same rights as before. git status is clean.

After the restart, 72 jobs matched again: kitstak revenue 175,169,952 and profit 53,074,581, northwind 158,278,720 and 53,544,441. Profit by job, client, site, service and month for Sep 1 to Nov 18 all total 165,516,613 revenue and 41,564,707 profit, the same as /summary and my SQL on v_facts.

category_scores.category: 2 Job costing and budget vs actual
category_scores.note: Job cost and profit now include warehouse extra services. On WO000091, a test record of 7 pallets at 14.50 moved job revenue from 15,400 to 25,550 cents and profit by the same 10,150. Contract rates set the unit price of 5 linked jobs. The quote is not rewritten from the contract, so plan and price can come from two places.

The new day form saved 3 labor types in one go and the math was right: 30 x 26.25 + 2 x 35.60 + 8 x 33.21 + 10.5 x 29.40 = 1,433.08. 10 parallel saves of one row gave one 200 and nine 409. Holes: the bulk save takes a row with no version, merges two lines of the same labor type without a word, and a work date in 2030 is saved.

All 1,571 work rows have labor cost equal to hours times the stamped rate plus overtime. v_facts, fact_days and job_stats agree for every job and for every kind in both orgs, before and after each sync I ran.

Alert rules now hide every line from no money roles: 14 of 14 rules come back with threshold null and moneyHidden true, and the page has no dollar or percent line. It also hides lines that are not money, like the count of days with nothing logged.

/profit/facts now pages: 4,062 rows over 6 pages, no repeats, per kind sums equal to SQL. CSV exports guard text against formulas (=, +, -, @ and a leading tab all got a quote mark). New leak: clients.csv, jobs.csv and job_types.csv show target margin percent to no money roles.

WMS extra services flow in: 13 records, 13 entries, 75,350 cents, each price equal to the record total or count times contract rate. Projects time flows in and is taken out when deleted. Limits: only the first rate tier is read, work order fees ignore tiers and dates, there is no off switch, and a new warehouse service record sends no change note, so Pulse sees it on the next stale sync, up to about 10 to 15 minutes later.

Refusals read well, for example 'Harbor Roast Collectiv looks like Harbor Roast Collective, a client you already have.' Connected apps says in plain words that 3 service entries have no price and what to do. Delete of a whole work day is one tap with no ask first, only an Undo.

50 pages for each of 3 users loaded with no console error, no server error and no CSP violation. The day form fits a 768 px tablet with no side scroll, but all 36 of its controls are under 40 px tall and the edit and delete buttons are 28 by 28. Not my main lens.

Better: a nonce CSP with no eval, 46 RLS policies that I proved with my own plain role, 775 tests green 3 runs in a row, the kiosk test green 12 of 12. Still weak: no CI at all, and the app connects as a superuser and never sets pulse.org_id, so the policies do not guard the running app.

round_two_issues_rechecked.title: No CI, no CSP, and RLS turned on with zero policies
round_two_issues_rechecked.evidence: Partly fixed. CSP is on every page: default-src 'self', script-src with a fresh nonce and strict-dynamic, no unsafe-eval, frame-ancestors 'none', object-src 'none'. 150 page loads showed 0 violations. RLS: pg_policies has 46 policies on 46 tables, and v_facts is security_invoker. My own role se_probe saw 0 rows in all 46 tables and the view with no setting, could not insert, saw 12,631 rows of only kitstak with the kitstak setting (4,324 facts rows, 1 org), 2,763 facts rows of only northwind with that setting, and got an error on a bad uuid. Still open: there is no .github folder, so nothing runs the tests on a change. And the app role is postgres, a superuser, and the code never sets pulse.org_id, so the policies do not protect the running app. The CSP has no report address, allows inline styles and any https image.

Delete of a whole day is one tap with no ask first. The edit and delete buttons are 28 by 28 px and sit side by side. I deleted a day by mistake in my own test.

blocking_issues.title: The day save can lose hours: no version needed, and same labor type lines are merged

blocking_issues.why_it_matters: The single row route refuses a missing version with 409, so the two write paths do not agree. On the bulk path a second writer can still win without a warning, and a pasted sheet with two rows for one crew loses the first row's hours and cost.

blocking_issues.title: Work can be dated years ahead

blocking_issues.why_it_matters: A typed 2062 instead of 2026 puts units and revenue in a month nobody looks at, and the row looks like a normal day in the list.

blocking_issues.title: The contract rate rule is narrow and has no off switch
blocking_issues.repro: Read with the live data: work order fees use standard_rate only and ignore billing_fee_tiers. The newest approved contract wins by calc_start_date with no check that it has started. Service rates take the lowest tier whatever the count. Fees with conditions are skipped. The first time a contract is seen the price is written from 0001-01-01, so every open month of the job is repriced, including on completed jobs. A changed warehouse service record sends no change note: my test record was not picked up by 4 cron ticks in a row because the last sync was under 10 minutes old.
blocking_issues.why_it_matters: For a client with volume tiers or a contract that starts next month, Pulse revenue will not match the warehouse bill, and an admin cannot turn the rule off for one job. The round three notes admit the missing switch and that the quote is not rewritten.

blocking_issues.title: Deleted jobs are open to a supervisor through the jobs list flag
blocking_issues.repro: As j.okafor: GET /api/v1/jobs/deleted answers 403. GET /api/v1/jobs?deleted=1 answers 200 and includes the deleted job J-1045. GET /api/v1/jobs/J-1045 also still answers 200 after the delete.
blocking_issues.why_it_matters: The new Deleted jobs list is meant for managers. The same rows are one query flag away for any role. No money is shown, so it is small, but the guard is not in one place.

best_things: Warehouse money now flows in and is safe to run again. One entry per record, the right price from the record or the contract, updates and removals follow the warehouse, and closed months are left alone.
The numbers still tie out. Raw rows, v_facts, fact_days, job_stats and the API agreed for every job in both orgs each time I checked, including right after each sync.
Row level security is real for a plain role. My own role saw 0 rows with no setting and only one org with it, through tables and through the facts view.
Concurrency holds. 10 parallel updates gave one winner and nine 409s with the fresh row. 10 parallel creates of one new line gave one row.
The CSP is a proper nonce policy with no eval, and 150 page loads had no violation and no console error.
HTML and CSV are escaped. A job name with a script tag did nothing on 9 pages and 2 print pages, and formula starts got a quote mark in CSV.
Projects time in and out works, with the right hours, people and cost.
Delete and restore of a job is exact. Facts went from 20 rows to 0 and back to 20 with the same labor total, and other orgs and no money roles are refused.
Tests are steady: 775 of 775 three times, the kiosk test 12 of 12.
what_would_wow_me: Three things. First, run the app as a plain database role that sets pulse.org_id for each request, so the 46 policies guard every query, and add a CI workflow that runs typecheck, lint, the 775 tests and the Playwright suite on each push. Second, close the last money and guard gaps with one shared rule each: target margin hidden in every export and page payload, the look alike check inside the one function that makes a client, a version needed on every write path, and a limit on how far ahead a work date can be. Third, make the contract rule honest about the warehouse bill: read tiers and start dates, show which contract set a price, and give a switch per job. With the first one done I would sign the security review.
verdict_paragraph: Round three fixed six of my seven round two issues, and I proved each one on the running system. The biggest one is real: warehouse extra services and contract rates now reach Pulse money, with no doubles on a second sync, with updates and removals that follow the warehouse, and with every total still matching the raw rows to the cent. Projects time now flows in and out. The facts route pages, the kiosk test is steady, alert lines are hidden, and there is a good CSP. The seventh is only partly done. The row level security policies work for a plain role, but the app connects as a superuser and never sets the org setting, so they guard nothing in practice, and there is still no CI. I also found a new small money leak, target margin in three exports and one page payload, and a few places where the server trusts the screen: look alike clients, the bulk day save and future dates. Pulse is a better engineered and more open product than Easy Metrics for a kitting shop, 85 against an estimated 52. I am not wowed yet, because the last line of defence for tenant data is still application code alone.

lens: Principal product designer, enterprise UX. I judged visual quality, match with the sibling KitStak apps, hierarchy, navigation, the daily entry flow, responsive behavior at 1440, 768 and 390, dark mode, accessibility, console errors, layout shift and 8th grade copy. I tested the running production build at localhost:3500 with Playwright 1.63 and @axe-core/playwright (wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21aa), installed in my own scratch folder. Sweep: 35 routes at 1440 and 390 in light and dark and at 768 in light, as admin@kitstak.io and again as the supervisor j.okafor@kitstak.io. That is 350 page loads with axe, console capture, overflow check and a layout shift observer on each. I then drove the flows by hand in scripts: quick add, the delete dialog, the Deleted tab, restore, undo, the client picker in three places with keyboard only, Plan vs actual, the log grid, the month close card, the job profit report, an extra service ledger with warehouse rows, alert rules as the supervisor, and the PR 37 day form. I signed in to CRM, Projects, WMS and Portal once and compared header, type and buttons. Easy Metrics scores are the public evidence estimates from competitors.md section 5. I did not test Easy Metrics hands on. Not tested: a real screen reader (I read the ARIA names and roles from the DOM), real touch devices, the import round trip, the rate builder, and email (deferred, noted once). Two other critics wrote to the same data while I worked, so I only compared numbers inside one page load. CLEANUP: I made one job, J-1043 UXCRIT3 temp job A, on Harbor Roast Collective. I logged, edited and deleted test days on it for Nov 17 and Nov 18, then deleted the job in the UI. It now sits soft deleted in Jobs, Deleted, with 3 soft deleted entries and 0 live ones. I made no clients. Nothing else is left behind. Scripts, logs and screenshots are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-kitstak-platform/ce6bf3e7-8fe5-5b33-baf8-b66b85d8f93e/scratchpad/critics/ux/ .

blocking_issues.title: Month close card and Target pace fail axe
blocking_issues.where: /settings/close as admin (all widths, both themes), /target-pace as supervisor at 390 and 768
blocking_issues.repro: Run axe with wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21aa. /settings/close gives 3 rules on 5 of 5 loads: aria-valid-attr-value (critical) on the selected tab 'Company costs', whose aria-controls points to an id that is not on the page (all 5 tabs point to missing ids), definition-list (serious) on dl[data-testid=close-job-side], and dlitem (serious) on 4 dt and dd nodes such as 'Revenue'. /target-pace as j.okafor gives scrollable-region-focusable (serious) on a div.overflow-x-auto at 390 light, 390 dark and 768 light.
blocking_issues.why_it_matters: The month close card is new in this round and it shipped with a critical ARIA error. Screen reader users get a tab that goes nowhere and a broken list for the main money numbers. It breaks the clean axe record: 342 of 350 loads pass, not 350.

blocking_issues.title: Month close says 'Ready to close' and 'needs fixing' at the same time
blocking_issues.repro: Open /settings/close and pick October 2026. The chip next to the title says 'Ready to close'. The line under it says '1 step needs fixing before these numbers can be trusted.' The checklist row 'Every extra service has a price' carries a red 'Fix this first' chip. The big red 'Close the month' button is live the whole time.
blocking_issues.why_it_matters: Three signals pull three ways. An owner cannot tell if it is safe to lock the month. The status should say 'One thing to fix' until the red step is done, or the button should say what happens if you close anyway.

blocking_issues.title: Content jumps on first paint on about one page load in thirteen
blocking_issues.repro: Load each page with a PerformanceObserver for layout-shift. 26 of 350 loads scored over 0.1, the line Google calls needs work. Worst cases: /labor as supervisor 0.48 at 768, 0.35 at 390, 0.31 at 1440. /target-pace as admin 0.40 at 768 and 0.28 at 390. /services as admin 0.29 at 390 and 0.21 at 1440 (table rows move at about 390 ms and 460 ms). /reports/job-profit 0.17 at 390. /settings/audit 0.17 at 390. /log/entries 0.15 at 390. /alerts as supervisor 0.17 at 390. Home is 0.
blocking_issues.why_it_matters: Home was fixed, but the same streaming pattern still moves cards and rows under the pointer on other pages. On a phone that means mis-taps. It reads as unfinished.

blocking_issues.title: Native selects and native date boxes are still mixed with KitStak pickers
blocking_issues.repro: Count visible native controls. /log: 31 select elements for labor class, next to a KitStak Site picker. /log/bulk: 2 selects, 'Job to fill' and 'Job for the row on Nov 18'. /jobs/new: 2 input type=date, Start date and Due date. /jobs/J-1012/work: 1 input type=date for Day, shown as 11/18/2026.
blocking_issues.why_it_matters: This is the round one item, still open after two rounds, and it spread to the new form. The browser chevron and the browser calendar look and act unlike every other picker in the suite, and the date format changes from 'Wed, Nov 18' to '11/18/2026' between two screens for the same job.

blocking_issues.title: A row with units and no hours shows 'margin 100%' and lifts the day's margin
blocking_issues.repro: On /log, on a job row with nothing logged (I used J-1043, price $1.25), type Units good 100 and People 4, leave the hours empty. The chip says 'Add the hours each' and right under it 'Labor $0.00, margin 100%'. It saves. The footer went from Earned today $33,139.05 and Margin today 45.9% to $33,264.05 and 46.1%.
blocking_issues.why_it_matters: Round one fixed a new job claiming a 100% margin. The same false number is back at row level, and it flows into the day total. A row that is missing hours should say 'No margin yet' and stay out of the day margin until it is whole.

blocking_issues.title: Client picker error feedback is clumsy and differs by screen
blocking_issues.where: /jobs quick add strip, /log 'Add a job' dialog
blocking_issues.repro: Strip: type 'Harbor', Tab, fill the other three boxes, press Enter. The list drops open on top of the red message, so only the tail '...choose Create "Harbor".' can be read. The input has aria-invalid=true but no aria-describedby. Dialog: do the same in 'Add a job'. The message is different ('Pick a client from the list, or choose Create to add a new one.'), it sits at the bottom of the dialog, the Client box gets no red border and aria-invalid stays null, and the list reopens over Job name, Units planned and Price while keyboard focus is still in the hidden Job name box. The labels also differ: 'Units to make' and 'Price per unit' in the strip, 'Units planned' and 'Price for each unit' in the dialog.
blocking_issues.why_it_matters: The look alike guard is the right fix, but the moment it fires is the moment the user most needs a clear message next to the right box. A screen reader user is not told which field is wrong. One picker should give one message in one place.

blocking_issues.title: Extra service with no cost and a missing price shows 'Margin 100%, Healthy'
blocking_issues.repro: Open the page as admin. Both entries are 'From the warehouse'. Cards read Revenue $195, Cost $0, Margin 100% with a green 'Healthy' chip, and '$0.00 to do one'. Below, 'Entries, 2. 1 entry has no price and earn nothing yet.' The Oct 22 row says 'No price' in red, but the text is not a button and the row has no action to set a price. 'From the warehouse' is a link to localhost:3000/billing/vas with no underline and grey text, rgb(89, 98, 116), so it does not look like a link.
blocking_issues.why_it_matters: Warehouse rows bring revenue with no labor, so the page calls the service perfect when Pulse does not know the cost at all. That is the wrong thing to tell an owner. It should say 'Cost not known yet', give a way to fix the price from the row, and show the link as a link. Also 'earn' should be 'earns'.

blocking_issues.title: Alert rules page tells a no money reader to do things the page does not offer
blocking_issues.repro: Sign in as the supervisor and open /alerts/rules. The text says 'You can change who gets told and turn one off. They cannot be deleted.' The page has 0 buttons, switches or inputs. There is no sign of which rules are on or off. The rule 'Tell me when an active job has nothing logged for a few work days', which 'Tells managers and supervisors', hides its day count too ('a few'), though days are not money. The API returns threshold null and moneyHidden true for it.
blocking_issues.why_it_matters: Hiding the dollar lines is right. But the copy was not rewritten for the read only view, and a supervisor who gets this alert cannot see how many days trigger it. Show the day count, show on or off, and drop the line about changing rules.

best_things: All seven round two blockers are fixed in the running app. I could not make any of them come back.

The delete flow is now how it should be: a clear dialog that names the job and what leaves the reports ('$28,600 of revenue and 800.5 labor hours'), safe focus on 'Keep the job', a landing on the Jobs list, an Undo toast, and a Deleted tab with who, when and a Restore button named for each job.

The client picker is a proper combobox with full keyboard use: arrows, Enter to pick, Esc closes only the list inside a dialog, 'Did you mean' first, 'Create' second. It caught every look alike I tried, including a typo and a missing 'Co.'
350 page loads with 0 console errors, 0 hydration warnings, 0 CSP violations, 0 failed requests and 0 sideways page overflow, across two roles, three widths and both themes.
The supervisor saw 0 dollar signs on 175 page loads, and the new delete dialog, Work tab and alert rules all keep money out for that role.
Plan vs actual on a tablet is now clean label and value cards with the projected numbers whole.
The month close bridge from job profit to company profit is easy to follow and the numbers add up to the cent.
The multi labor type day form does the hard parts right: correct overtime math, one line per day, atomic saves, whole day delete with Undo.
Pulse still looks like one family with CRM, Projects and WMS: same 56 px header, wordmark, Inter type, red 32 px buttons and 12 px card corners. Dark mode is clean on every route.
what_would_wow_me: I would sign when these are done. One: 'Add a day of work' never replaces a day without asking, and every save there has Undo. Two: no table hides money columns or row actions. Pin the last columns or switch to cards under 1024 like Plan vs actual does, and give every scroll box a name, a tab stop and a fade. The Job profit table must show Profit at 1440. Three: axe clean on 350 of 350, which means fixing the month close tabs and list and the Target pace scroll box. Four: the labor class, job and date pickers become KitStak pickers everywhere, so the round one item finally closes. Five: no page scores over 0.1 for layout shift. Reserve the space like Home now does. Six: no screen ever prints 'margin 100%' or 'Healthy' when cost or hours are missing. Seven: one name for each thing: Labor type, Units to make, Price per unit, Job profit. Eight: month close status that does not say ready and not ready at once. None of this is a redesign. It is the last layer of finish on a product that is already well ahead of the Easy Metrics baseline.
verdict_paragraph: Round three did what it said on the seven things I blocked on. Delete is safe and can be undone. The client picker stops look alikes and works by keyboard. Plan vs actual is whole on a tablet. The hours check agrees with the row. There are two margin names. The $21K client level loss has its own plain panel. Hydration errors are gone and Home no longer jumps. I checked each one by hand and could not break it. Across 350 page loads as admin and supervisor I saw 0 console errors and 0 page overflow, and axe passed on 342. So Pulse is the better product against the Easy Metrics estimate of 52, and I raise my score from 85 to 87. I am not wowed, because the new work brought new rough edges that I would not put my name on yet. The new day form on the job Work tab replaces a day that is already logged without asking, and that loses real production data. Two tables still hide their most important columns or their Edit and Delete buttons with no cue, one of them the Profit column on the Job profit report at 1440. The new month close card fails axe with a critical ARIA error and tells the owner the month is ready and not ready in the same card. Native selects from round one are still on the log grid, and native date boxes came back in the wizard and the new form. Several pages still jump on load, up to 0.48. And two screens print 'margin 100%' when the cost is simply not known. These are all small, exact fixes. One more round at this pace gets a yes with no caveats.
